blocks.path: What is AMD? - Age-related macular degeneration (AMD)
s: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a common condition that affects the middle part of your vision.
It usually first affects people in their 50s.

blocks.path: What is AMD? - Age-related macular degeneration (AMD)
s: It does not cause total blindness, but it can make things like reading and recognising faces difficult.

blocks.path: What is AMD? - Age-related macular degeneration (AMD)
s: Without treatment, your vision may get worse.
This can happen gradually over several years, before it can then get worse quickly over a few weeks or months.

blocks.path: What is AMD? - Age-related macular degeneration (AMD)
s: It's been linked to things such as ageing, smoking, high blood pressure, being overweight and having a family history of AMD.
